answers.core:
This design pattern is a commonly used in data driven games and many people coming from other engines expect to be able to do it. 

Look up "Godot resource duplication" or "Godot node duplication" and just about all you will find are people who are confused about why this isn't Godot's default functionality. It's literally every result on the first page aside from Godot's documentation as I write this.

We can't expect Godot to be the same as the engines we came from but there is simply no substitution for this design pattern that I've been able to find that is reasonable for someone who's programming ability is limited to scripting.
answers.workaround: The only workaround I've found is instantiating a new version of the base resource that doesn't exist yet, then manually copying all variables from the duplicated resource to the new one. With every change that is made to any object that needs to be duplicated changes to the duplication code are thus required and this is the only workaround I've managed to find through forums and tutorials.

title: Add a Force Unique property to Resource that forces duplication on copy even in the same scene
